prompts: The owner's gaming rig hitches every few seconds even though the average frame rate looks fine, and the 1% lows are poor. A one-minute frame capture, a sensor log, a dump of the rig's settings and the owner's notes are in {WS}. That rig is not this machine: everything about it is in these files, and nothing is to be applied to this host. Find what causes the hitches and which setting changes fix them within the owner's constraints. Record in {WS}/result.json: avg_fps, low_1pct_fps, cause and changes (a list of {setting, from, to}).
answers:
[goal] Find the hitch cause and the fix; record in ./result.json.
[action] Parsed the 1-min PresentMon capture (8238 frames) and 60 s sensor log, cross-referenced the frame-time spikes against per-second sensors.
[result] avg_fps = 137.3; low_1pct_fps = 45.4 (p99 frame time 22.05 ms). Cause: GPU PCIe ASPM L1 on the GPU RP — every ~4 s the link drops to L1 (sensor samples at s=2,6,10,...,58) and ~12 frames jump to ~21–23 ms each. `pcie_aspm_rp1_gpu: L1 → disabled` fixes it, keeping Gen5 x4 link speed/width and BIOS overclock settings untouched. The Defender scan spikes at s=43–45 (MsMpEng, DPC 420–455 µs) are one-off and show no frame drops, so no change made for them. Written to result.json.
[next] Apply the setting change on the rig (BIOS), then re-capture to verify the L1 hitches are gone; optionally add defender exclusions for the game folder, and re-check rp0 nvme L1 only if future captures show disk-related hitches.

Assumptions: 1% low computed as 1000 / p99 of MsBetweenPresents per the owner's definition; hitch frames = >15 ms; the "every few seconds" pattern is what the 1% low captures. No browser tabs or windows were opened, so nothing to close.
